messages:
lucas: FYI found a weird edgecase in the .NET SDK + JSON mode when using function calls with streaming: partial JSON fragments from the tool can be merged and the schema validator accepts the result by silently repairing a trailing-comma, which then produces a different object shape for the app. blocked a new customer onboarding flow.

maya: whoa. never heard of a validator auto-fixing trailing commas. can you share repro?

lucas: quick repro: starter-dotnet in JSON mode, function_call 'list_sessions' expects an array of objects. Our proxy tool streams chunks: first chunk '[{"id":"s1", "meta": {"t":1}},' then later chunk ' {"id":"s2","meta":{"t":2}}]' but due to a small broker bug a chunk arrives with an extra comma: ' ,'. The SDK's streaming assembler concatenates chunks and the schema helper attempts a quick repair: it strips the duplicate comma and parses, returning the array. The app downstream relies on the exact ordering and metadata and fails because the helper also flattened nested meta keys during a second pass (coercion helper).

Example payload sent to model:```json
{"model":"rw-dotnet-1","mode":"json","function_call":{"name":"list_sessions","arguments_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"limit":{"type":"integer"}}}}}
```

logs:```
[2026-03-30T11:45:01Z] WARN stream-assembler: saw consecutive comma tokens, attempting repair
[2026-03-30T11:45:01Z] INFO schema-shim: permissive-repair applied (trailing/comma)
[2026-03-30T11:45:01Z] WARN shim-coerce: flattening nested 'meta' object to top-level keys
[2026-03-30T11:45:01Z] ERR app: session ordering mismatch - expected s1 then s2
```

dev-support: Not good. SDK helper should not mutate structure in a way that changes semantics. Repairs are OK for harmless whitespace, but flattening nested keys is a no-go. Also repairs should be opt-in and clearly logged.

maya: Agreed. Two mitigations: 1) quick patch in starter-dotnet to set env var `REDWOOD_DOTNET_PERMISSIVE_PARSE=false` to force strict parsing so the app sees the parse error instead of a mutated payload, 2) change the SDK helper to limit repairs to syntax-only fixes (remove duplicate commas/brackets) and never perform structural coercions like flattening. Add an opt-in `PERMISSIVE_SCHEMA_SHIM=true` for old customers.

lucas: I pushed the sample patch with the env var and a small reproducer; customer unblocked. Also attached the minimal broker reproduction gist to the ticket.

ci-bot: CI: starter-samples/dotnet-test failed for `stream-fragment-repair` (https://ci/c/13421) :red_circle:

eric: I'll open a dotnet-sdk PR to change the helper: - stop flattening nested objects during shimning - only allow syntax repairs with a whitelist - emit a clear telemetry event when repairs happen. Also add an integration test in starter-samples that simulates duplicate-comma fragments.

maya: good. let's also add a cross-SDK note in the parity doc stating that repairs are syntax-only and structural coercion is disallowed. We saw too many subtle app bugs from silent structural changes.

dev-support: I'll notify the onboarding customer with the env var workaround and ETA for the SDK patch (24-48h). Also recommend they pin the starter sample version until patch release.

lucas: thanks. once the PR is in I'll add the reproducer to the PR so support can easily run it locally. :thumbsup:

eric: PR opened: https://repo/rw/dotnet-sdk/pull/88 - includes tests + telemetry. Plan to cut 1.4.1 patch after CI green.

maya: good catch, lucas. This should keep the starter flow predictable for new partners.
